public_body: University Of Massachusetts Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the UMass Board violated the Open Meeting Law throughout the presidential search, including improper executive sessions, telephone participation, and deficient notices and minutes, and ordered training and records release.

allegations.summary: Board held a three-hour executive session on Jan 13, 2011 to interview presidential finalists and discuss their qualifications, rather than in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the interviews and discussion should have taken place in open session.

allegations.summary: Board cited 'reputation and character' (Purpose 1) to hold closed discussion of finalists' professional competence and the final consensus on the president.
allegations.key_passage: Rather, the evidence demonstrates that the Board attempted to force very real and pertinent questions about professional competence into the rubric of "reputation and character" so that the interviews and debate could be conducted behind closed doors.

allegations.summary: Board cited strategy for non-union negotiations (Purpose 2) and compliance with law (Purpose 7) as executive session grounds without applicable basis.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board did not provide any law or grant-in-aid requirement to justify their executive session under Purpose 7, it was not appropriate for the Board to employ Purpose 7.

allegations.summary: Search Committee and Board members participated by telephone in meetings in November 2010 and January 2011, when remote participation was not permitted.
allegations.key_passage: While it is not clear from either the minutes or our interviews to what extent the members participated, each instance of remote participation constitutes a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Search Committee held executive sessions on Oct-Dec 2010 and Jan 2011 as 'continuations' of the Sept 17 session without posting separate notice for each meeting.
allegations.key_passage: This practice violates the explicit notice requirement of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Search Committee convened executive sessions as continuations without first convening in open session, taking a roll-call vote, or stating purpose before each session.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Search Committee's practice of merely "continuing" the executive session from one date to another denied the public that knowledge.

allegations.summary: Search Committee minutes of its September 2010 and executive interview sessions were too brief, lacking discussion summaries, votes, and documents used.
allegations.key_passage: Meeting minutes, whether for open or executive sessions, must give the reader an adequate understanding of what actually happened at the meeting.

allegations.summary: Notices for the Sept 17, 2010 Search Committee meeting and the Jan 13, 2011 Board meeting lacked an adequate listing of topics the chair anticipated discussing.
allegations.key_passage: This was a significant action by the Board, and clearly anticipated by the chair.

allegations.summary: A Search Committee subgroup that reviewed and selected a search firm, meeting without notice or minutes, was alleged to be a subcommittee subject to the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Whether or not this group was loosely organized, or conducted its work informally with the assistance of staff, it was nonetheless a subcommittee subject to the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25; similar future violations will be considered intentional.
Certify to the Division that each Board member has received a copy of the determination.
Undergo Open Meeting Law training, conducted by an approved attorney or organization, before beginning the appointment of a new UMass Amherst Chancellor, and certify attendance by every member.
Submit to the Division copies of all required meeting notices posted by the Board or its subcommittees during the chancellor appointment process.
Submit to the Division all open and executive session minutes created during the chancellor appointment process.
Review all unreleased executive session minutes from the presidential search and release those where the purpose for confidentiality no longer exists, within 60 days.
Create, approve, and release full and accurate minutes for the Search Committee's September 17, October 7, October 8, October 21, October 22, and November 3, 2010 meetings.
remedy_passage: Therefore, among other requirements and as discussed more fully below, we order the Board to undergo Open Meeting Law training before it begins the process of appointing a new chancellor.
